message.content: {"caption":"Memory examples paired with a line chart comparing successful-task counts as tested tasks increase.","description":"A composite figure has three memory cards on the left and a line chart on the right. The first card, “Trajectory Memory,” shows a user icon and a recorded interaction: clicking “My Account,” reasoning that the “Recent Orders” section is not enough to find the first purchase, then using “View All” to open the full order history. A later thought describes the “My Orders” page, where orders are displayed newest to oldest, followed by another click action. The second card, “Workflow Memory,” is titled “Retrieve Information from Specific Page Section”; its example describes accessing a specific section, clicking a section or tab, and sending the extracted information to the user. The third card, “ReasoningBank Memory,” contains a “Navigation Strategy” with a description about searching history for specific information and a partially shown content list: detect the page mode and examine relevant orders; avoid infinite scrolls and use fallbacks if the primary mode fails; and cross-reference with common … . The text in these cards includes ellipses and is partly truncated. The chart plots “Number of Tested Tasks” from 0 to 40 on the horizontal axis and “Number of Successful Tasks” from 0 to 18 on the vertical axis. The gray “ReasoningBank” and light-blue “No Memory” lines both rise overall from near zero, with fluctuations; ReasoningBank is generally above No Memory and finishes near 15 successful tasks versus about 12. Callouts with small icons mark “Top-3 best-selling products in Jan 2023,” “Best-selling product type in Jan 2023,” “Top-2 searches in the store,” “Earliest order for customer,” “Grand total of invoice,” “Num of reviews mentioning ‘decent’,” and monthly counts of top-3 products for 01/2023–05/2023 in MM:COUNT format. Two unlabeled red dashed arrows point out toward the upper-left and lower-left from the plot area.
